# jamfplatform_pro_jamf_pro_server_url (Data Source)

Reads the Jamf Pro server URL (Settings > Jamf Pro Server URL), the URL devices check in against. One value per tenant. Read-only; reference the returned `url` elsewhere in your configuration, such as in enrollment URLs, webhooks, or scripts.

**Required Jamf permissions**

Create the API integration with **Platform environment** scope (preferred) or **Tenant** scope, then grant it the following permissions in Jamf Account — see [Getting started with the Platform API](https://developer.jamf.com/platform-api/reference/getting-started-with-platform-api). `Category` and `Permission` name the section and row of the permission picker; `Actions` are the boxes to tick within that row.

| Category | Permission | Actions | API capability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | Jamf Pro server URL | Read | `jss-url` |

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read the Jamf Pro server URL that devices check in against.
data "jamfplatform_pro_jamf_pro_server_url" "current" {}

output "jamf_pro_server_url" {
  value = data.jamfplatform_pro_jamf_pro_server_url.current.url
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Fixed singleton identifier. Always `singleton`.
- `url` (String) The Jamf Pro server URL that devices check in against.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
